svg.title: The factor 2n+1 pays the real-and-imaginary expansions of the n inserted directions and the one tested input direction. Conversion of the finitely many color coordinates to their Euclidean norm multiplies these by √n1 and √n0, respectively. For the emission the probability-average estimate is a sum of squares divided by L4; removing that denominator and taking a square root contributes exactly L2. Taking the maximum, or the larger finite sum, over n = 0, 1, 2 gives prices a and h independent of L, with charter price a and emission price L2h. These are RealGap.CharterR.costs and Chromatic.costs. The same finite derivative and Fourier-frame bounds give the sector price
